title: Tenant-capacity-aware ingest throttler + signed-envelope proxy for VPC/on‑prem collectors
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Private and VPC collector endpoints occasionally get bursted by noisy tenants (large replay, bad SDK loops, or customer misconfiguration). On Dedicated pools this can cause head-of-line latency for other tenants and SLO violations. We currently have coarse per-collector admission controls, but they are insufficient for multi-tenant isolation in constrained on-prem footprints.

Goal:
Implement a lightweight, tenant-aware ingest throttler that operates at the collector perimeter (either sidecar or perimeter forwarder) which: (1) enforces soft and hard per-tenant ingest budgets and backpressure, (2) gracefully sheds or reroutes excessive traffic to a preconfigured fallback (shared-burst-relay or delayed replay buffer), and (3) signs telemetry envelopes (HMAC) for downstream audit and replay integrity. The system must preserve trace/span correlation headers and sampling decisions so that observability data remains usable for latency/error dashboards and incident playbooks.

Non-goals:
- Full billing-level metering (handled by billing pipeline).
- Replacing the long-term storage replay system (we will integrate with existing replay components).

Acceptance criteria:
- Collector can enforce per-tenant soft limit (configurable e.g., tokens/min) and hard limit (requests/min) with observable metrics (throttled_count, rerouted_count, allowed_count) per tenant.
- When a tenant exceeds soft limit, packets are delayed (HTTP 202 + Retry-After or queued internally) rather than dropped; when exceeding hard limit, events are rerouted to fallback with signed envelope.
- Signed envelopes use HMAC-SHA256 with key rotation capability; verifier in replay/ingest accepts signatures and records verification result metric.
- Trace context (traceparent / baggage / x-cloud-trace) preserved end-to-end for samples forwarded to primary or fallback.
- Dashboard with per-tenant ingest latency P50/P95, error rate, backlog size, and fallback traffic shown in Console; alert if >5% of total traffic is rerouted for 5m.
- End-to-end tests and a canary rollout plan exist; collectors can be rolled back without data loss.

Design notes:
- Throttler implemented as a small Go process embedded in the perimeter forwarder and as an optional sidecar mode for airgapped clusters. Use token-bucket per-tenant with refill rates derived from tenant SLA config stored in central config-service (cached locally).
- For high-cardinality tenants we maintain a bounded LRU of active tenant buckets and aggregate the rest into a tenant-fallback-bucket to avoid unbounded memory growth.
- Fallback options (configurable per-deployment): (A) relay to a shared burst ingestion pool (Dedicated fallback), (B) write to local encrypted replay buffer with watermarking for later replay. Both paths attach a signed envelope containing metadata: tenant_id, original_timestamp, sequence_id, signature_version.
- Use a well-defined envelope schema (v1) and include a tenant-origin header for downstream filtering. Signing key managed by KMS integration (if available) or local key-ring with rotation cron.

Operational/observability integration:
- Emit metrics via our existing metrics client with labels: tenant_id, collector_id, action (allow/delay/reroute/drop), reason_code.
- Span instrumentation: start a short-lived span for throttler decisions with attributes: tenant.id, throttle.result, queue_time_ms, fallback_target. Spans should be linked to incoming traceparent when present.
- Logs: structured JSON logs for throttled events including sample payload hash (not payload) and signature metadata for audit. Logs must redact PII.
- Dashboards: add a per-cluster tile showing top 20 tenants by reroute rate and a global alert rule: reroute_ratio > 0.05 for 5m -> page SRE + oncall owner.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Feature flag gated in perimeter forwarder (off by default). Deploy to internal staging and run synthetic load tests.
2) Enable sidecar mode for two low-risk customers to validate onprem key handling and replay behavior.
3) Canary: enable in 10% of dedicated-edge forwarders for 24h with detailed telemetry (trace sampling x5).
4) Gradually increase to 100% over two weeks; if reroute ratio spikes unexpectedly, automatic rollback triggers.

Testing:
- Unit tests for token-bucket, signature generation/verification, envelope schema compatibility.
- E2E test: simulate noisy tenant, assert prioritized tenants see <10% latency regression and noisy tenant traffic ends up in fallback with signature verification passing.
- Chaos tests: intermittent KMS failures should fall back to local key-ring; record metric kms_fallback_count.

Security notes:
- Signatures prevent accidental data mixup during replay and provide chain-of-custody. Key access limited to collector service principal and KMS.
- Ensure no secret keys written to logs. Use HSM/KMS where possible.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Memory vs accuracy: LRU sketch will reduce per-tenant accuracy for low-volume tenants. Is occasional misattribution acceptable? PM thinks yes for initial iteration.
- Fallback durability: local replay buffer must be encrypted and have bounded retention; how do we surface quota overages to customers? Suggest embedding metadata in Console usage view (later PR).

References / links:
- design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/tenant+throttler+v1 (placeholder)
- proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proto/pulls/1234
- related tickets: ENG-41207 (observability-handoff-protocol-for-dedicated-vpc), ENG-34001 (satellite-telemetry-bridge)
